name: files-viewer
title: Files Viewer
description: A folder's files in a viewer, as a file manager has them, four ways: a tree of rows with when each changed and its size, a description after a name, a status letter after a changed file's, ignored ones dimmed; a grid of thumbnails (images' own, the rest their type's icon) with a caption and a badge; columns of folder after folder with the picked file's preview, folding away with no room; and a gallery of the picked file large over a strip. Sorted by any column, or in the app's order; in the app's groups under headings. One picked, the arrow keys moving it as each view has them, Enter to open; a filter by name keeps the folders on the way open; the filter takes the path's place in the toolbar, and the app's own search's results are a flat list, each with where it is, how many said in the field. Search selects the first available result, shows its Open hint, and keeps focus in the field while Up and Down move selection and Enter opens it. The field replaces the search tool; its clear button closes it. The status bar shows the search folder, keyboard hints and results shown out of the supplied item count, preserving app controls and details. Only the rows in view are drawn, in the list and in each column. Folders loading, the files, previews and what opening does are the app's. A row may carry what a change adds and removes (+n −n) after its status. Disabled entries remain visible for context, skip selection and opening, and are passed by the keys in every view. The list leaves out a Modified or Size column no loaded file has; start puts the app's control in the path's place. The count prop optionally counts only the filtered top level for item and changed facts, preserving search result totals. levelFilter filters one folder's enabled files by name prefix, as a typed path's last segment does, driven by the app's input with no field opened: the other levels stay whole, the status bar says n of m items, a level with none says No matches; the toolbar's filter, while it has text, takes precedence. tree={false} shows a flat top-level list; openOn="click" opens on tap, onUp asks for the parent, and loading shows a spinner while files arrive. header={false} drops the list's column header and filter={false} the toolbar's filter; count can name one folder to count. A disabled entry takes no focus unless all are; one column alone keeps a column's width. Rows are 44px tall under a coarse pointer. It has no fill of its own: it takes the surface it sits on, a dialog's or a card's. Columns resize at each border with a fine pointer: drag, arrow keys or Home/End; double click or Enter resets. Widths by depth use columnWidths/defaultColumnWidths/onColumnWidthsChange; the fit count follows.
